newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Resilient NZ share market ends only mildly down.
newsitem.headline: Resilient NZ share market ends only mildly down.

text.p: * NZ shares fall only mildly despite interest rate rise
* Heavy turnover in Telecom and Fletcher letter stocks

Brokers marvelled at the slight fall on the New Zealand share market on Friday as it defied a heavy drop on Wall Street, an impending general election next month, higher bond yields and a weak Australian market.

"In a sense, we are defying gravity," said Cavill White's Don Turkington. "It's a remarkable good close to the week especially when you take into account rising interest rates, and an election in a little over a month's time," he said.
The top 40 index closed down 4.11 at 2231.82 on good volume of $81 million.
Telecom, down seven cents earlier, ended square at $6.98, and has confounded many with its strength against a rise in New Zealand long bonds to 8.50 from 8.0 percent in short order.

Turkington said the mood was buoyant with plenty of offshore interest. It had changed dramatically recently with a feeling that smaller parties would put a centre-right government in power after the October 12 election, he said.
However, not everyone is so sanguine. SBC Warburg broker John Rowley believes election jitters will dampen enthusiasm.
On market, apart from the $18.9 million turnover in Telecom, there was also heavy trade in Fletcher Building. The stock ended seven cents down on volume of 4.7 million shares.
Brokers were unsure why trade was so active, although they noted other Fletcher stocks were also heavily traded.
Sandford lost 10 cents to $2.50 in response to the sharp downturn in Sealord's profit announced with the Brierley result on Thursday.
Wrightson ended one cent up at $1.14 after announcing a sharply lower profit which had been well flagged.
